SMTO-TSK-0056 — The Agent pointed one step at two different computers

GUID: c4665a86-5363-49c1-b5d9-ff58f19392a8
Slug: dependency-target-conflict
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent named two different Gateways (the helper programs SMTO uses to run work on a computer) for one step. SMTO couldn't tell which you meant, so it rejected the plan and none of its steps ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at which Gateways are selected for your messages; they are shown with the message box. The Agent can only send steps to the Gateways you have selected.
  2. Wait to see whether the Agent tries again with a single computer for each step; it is told about this problem automatically. The Agent usually fixes a mixed-up target on its next attempt.
  3. If the task ends with this error, send a message naming the Gateway or computer each part of the work should run on, and ask the Agent to continue. None of the planned steps ran, so a clear instruction lets the Agent plan them again without repeating anything.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's steps start, each on the computer you named, and their results appear in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select extra Gateways just to get past this; that lets work run on computers you didn't intend.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • In an explicit parallel batch, an Activity's item-level target differs from the target field inside its child tool arguments, so the batch was rejected before any child was accepted.

What this means

  • An Activity's explicit target differs from the target inside its child tool arguments. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • An Activity's explicit target differs from the target inside its child tool arguments.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the outer activity target with the inner tool target and accepted Gateway selection.

How to fix it

  • Give each Activity exactly one target: set either the item-level target or the tool argument target (or make both identical), and use a Gateway that is among the run's selected targets. The rejection is returned to the model; re-plan with one unambiguous target per Activity.
  • Choose one unambiguous target representation within the named Gateway scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One consistent authorized target is used for the intended activity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
